skill.name: writing-skills
skill.description: Use when creating, editing, or verifying AI skills. It applies test-driven documentation and subagent pressure tests before deployment.
skill.summary: Create and verify AI skills with test-driven documentation practices.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts were false positives from Markdown fences, inline paths, or illustrative commands. I confirmed the hidden `~/.claude/skills` guidance as a security-sensitive persistence path and added a semantic finding for the optional git push deployment step. Manual review of `SKILL.zip` found it contains only a matching copy of `SKILL.md`.

remediation.issue: Persistent writes to hidden Claude skills directory
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before creating or editing files under `~/.claude/skills`; draft inside the workspace first when possible.

remediation.issue: Optional remote publication in deployment checklist
remediation.suggestion: Add a confirmation gate before any commit or push, and state which remote and branch will receive content.

remediation.issue: Duplicate zipped skill file reduces scanner visibility
remediation.suggestion: Remove SKILL.zip from the source tree or publish a checksum and archive listing with each release.

content.value_statement: Creating AI skills without testing can leave unclear instructions and hidden loopholes. This skill gives authors a test-driven process for drafting, pressure testing, and refining skill documentation.
actual_capabilities: Guides authors through a RED-GREEN-REFACTOR process for skill creation.
Explains skill naming, frontmatter, descriptions, and discovery terms.
Shows how to test skills with pressure scenarios and subagents.
Lists common rationalizations that cause untested skill changes.
References Anthropic skill guidance and persuasion principles for disciplined documentation.
limitations: Does not include executable validation scripts.
Depends on available subagent testing tools and user permissions.
Focuses on Claude-style skill authoring, not general technical writing.
Platform guidance may need updates when skill systems change.

use_cases.title: Create a New Skill
use_cases.description: Draft a focused skill with clear triggers, compact guidance, and a test plan before deployment.

use_cases.title: Review Skill Quality
use_cases.description: Check an existing skill for metadata quality, discovery terms, reference structure, and missing tests.

use_cases.title: Harden Discipline Rules
use_cases.description: Use pressure scenarios to find rationalizations and add explicit counters to process documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a New Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-skills to help me plan a new skill for [task]. Start with trigger conditions, scope, and a minimal SKILL.md structure.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill draft using writing-skills. Focus on description quality, search terms, structure, examples, and missing validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Pressure Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-skills to design pressure scenarios for this discipline-enforcing skill. Include baseline failure goals and pass criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor After Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-skills to interpret these subagent test results. Identify loopholes, rewrite the weak sections, and define the next verification cycle.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for handling flaky async tests.
output_examples.output: A concise skill plan with trigger conditions, core rule, testing scenarios, and a deployment checklist.
A prioritized review of metadata, discovery terms, structure, references, and missing validation tests.
Three scenario prompts, expected baseline failures, and revisions that address common rationalizations.

best_practices: Run a baseline scenario before writing or changing a skill.
Keep core instructions concise and move heavy reference material to separate files.
Retest after every change that closes a loophole.
anti_patterns: Writing a skill before observing the failure it must fix.
Adding many examples that dilute the main pattern.
Batching several skills without testing each one separately.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create and refine AI skills that document reusable techniques, patterns, tools, or reference material.

faq.question: Does it write the skill for me automatically?
faq.answer: It provides a process, checklists, and review criteria. The user still controls the final content and deployment.

faq.question: Why does it use test-driven development terms?
faq.answer: It treats documentation quality like code quality. Authors first observe failures, then write guidance, then retest.

faq.question: Can it help with existing skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review drafts, identify missing tests, and guide refactors after subagent results.

faq.question: Does it require Claude-specific tooling?
faq.answer: The content is written for Claude skills, but many documentation testing principles also apply to Codex and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I verify before deployment?
faq.answer: Verify trigger descriptions, metadata, reference links, pressure test results, and any file or repository changes.
